solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flask of rum or meths

indicators.note: rum is an old word for odd or strange, so the following letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's hip flask holds either rum or methylated spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' sits next to 'meths' as if it were another drink, but here it is the adjective meaning odd, telling you to rearrange OR METHS into THERMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum flask, the trade name having become the everyday word for any such insulated bottle.

clue.text: Discuss meat, but don't mince words

parts.note: to discuss is to talk
turkey is a kind of meat

explanation.surface: A conversation about meat, with a plea not to mince it, punning on minced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' plays on minced meat, but 'mince words' is the idiom for softening what you say.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is an idiom for speaking frankly and getting down to business, which is refusing to soften your language.

clue.text: Found in brasserie, a German very hungry

indicators.note: something found in a run of words is sitting inside them, waiting to be lifted out

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word, the article and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A ravenous German diner is spotted in a brasserie.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of brasserie through 'a' into the first three of German.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very hungry is keen and impatient for food, and eager means keenly wanting something.

clue.text: Staff produce vegetable

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
to produce something is to get it out

explanation.surface: A greengrocer's staff and their vegetable produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' reads as the noun for fresh vegetables, but it is the verb meaning bring out; 'Staff' is likewise a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout is a flat pea pod eaten whole, a common green vegetable in British shops.

clue.text: Extra bags seem, originally, meagre

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a spare is an extra one

indicators.note: originally points to where a word starts, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: opening letter of seem

explanation.surface: Extra luggage bags look thin and meagre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like a noun for luggage but is the verb meaning captures.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered or scanty, a close synonym of meagre for a small inadequate amount.

clue.text: Pool where idol swims

indicators.note: when your head swims everything moves about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes a dip at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swims' fits the pool so naturally that it is easy to miss it as the signal to rearrange IDOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, a term common in Britain for outdoor bathing places.

clue.text: Story line's not new

indicators.note: not tells you to go without something, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A storyline that turns out to be old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story line' reads as one word, storyline; split it, and 'Story' is the definition while 'line' loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A story can mean a fib, as when a child is told not to tell stories, so it is an untruth.

clue.text: When messy, stand up for cleaning receptacle

indicators.note: a messy state is a disordered one, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: When things get messy, stand up and fetch something to clean with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messy' fits the cleaning theme so neatly that it hides its role as the instruction to scramble STAND UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is the flat container into which you sweep dirt with a brush, so it holds sweepings while cleaning.

clue.text: Section of Wood's diary?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a piece cut from a tree trunk
second meaning: a daily record, as in a ship's

explanation.surface: An extract from the diary of someone called Wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital W makes Wood look like a person's surname, but it is just timber; the possessive is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a chunk of tree trunk and an official record kept day by day, such as a captain's journal.

clue.text: Northern area set to change Lebanon's region

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: things due to change will soon look different, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern part of Lebanon is due for some upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set to change' reads as a forecast of political change, but 'set' belongs to the letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is the older name for the countries of the eastern Mediterranean, the part of the world containing Lebanon.

clue.text: Perfect floor covering in use

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so a piece goes within the other

parts.note: to use up is to consume
a mat covers part of a floor

explanation.surface: Praise for the ideal flooring that is in use.
explanation.walkthrough: The mat goes between the last two letters of CONSUME.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means supremely skilled or complete in every respect, so it is a synonym of flawless.

clue.text: Short piece from scriptwriter selected

indicators.note: a piece from some words is a fragment cut out of them, letters lifted intact

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A brief extract is picked from a screenwriter's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short piece' looks like one phrase describing an extract, but 'Short' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and to the point, often curtly so, which is short in manner of speech.

clue.text: Sign is poor after treatment, having caught cold

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other
treatment works something over, so the letters come out reworked

parts.note: taken as written
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A patient's signs are poor after treatment because they caught a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'Sign' look like a symptom; it is a sign of the zodiac. The rearranged letters take C after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio, the scorpion, is one of the twelve astrological star signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Large ship, poor relation boarded by king

indicators.note: a vessel boarded by someone has them inside it, so one piece goes within another
something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king climbs aboard a big ship to visit a poor relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor relation' reads as a set phrase for an inferior cousin, but 'poor' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil tanker is a very big vessel built to carry crude oil in bulk across the oceans.

clue.text: Motive with respect to a family member

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
taken as written
a son is a member of a family

explanation.surface: A detective asks about the motive behind someone's treatment of a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Latin-derived 'in the matter of' seen at the top of business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the cause that drives someone to act, the grounds or rationale behind what they do.

clue.text: Sound of patient with cold: what might wipe nose, did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said something points to how words are heard rather than written

parts.note: a paper hanky is used to wipe a runny nose

explanation.surface: A doctor hears a cold sufferer and offers something to wipe their nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'a tissue' quickly and it becomes the British spelling of a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the British way of writing a sneeze, the noise someone suffering from a cold makes.

clue.text: Aircraft windows letting in minimum of light

indicators.note: letting something in admits it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: panes are sheets of window glass

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is the least you can take, a single opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of light

explanation.surface: Aircraft cabin windows let in very little light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aircraft' is the plural noun here, matching the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft can be plural, and planes is the everyday word for several flying machines with fixed wings.

clue.text: Not the first moment in time!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming next after the first in order
a sixtieth of a minute, or a brief instant

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes it read as one remark about time; split it into a position in a list and a tiny unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the ordinal after first in a sequence and a very short span of time, as in 'just a sec'.

clue.text: Letter tiles arranged by each person, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the words are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of each and person

indicators.note: arranging items puts them in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In a word game, each player sets out their letter tiles on the rack.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scrabble picture makes 'Letter' look like a tile; it is a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or literary written message, as in the epistles of the New Testament.

clue.text: Tea brought by idiot in the morning

parts.note: an ass is a fool
am is short for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A clumsy person brings a cup of tea at breakfast time.
explanation.walkthrough: AM is ante meridiem, Latin for before midday, as on a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea grown in the Indian state of the same name, popular as a breakfast brew.

clue.text: South American greeting Japanese dish

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation
US stands for the United States, so American
hi is an informal hello

explanation.surface: A South American welcome is served alongside a dish from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one adjective for a continent; split it into a compass point and the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is vinegared rice topped or rolled with raw fish, a famous food from Japan.

clue.text: Trefoil leaf in paste?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the three-lobed leaf that is Ireland's emblem

definitions.note: read as two words, a sham rock
definitions.meaning: second meaning: paste is glass made to imitate a gem, so a fake stone

explanation.surface: A clover leaf preserved in some kind of paste.
explanation.walkthrough: Paste here is imitation jewellery, and rock is slang for a diamond, so a fake gem is split into two words; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamrock is the small three-leaved clover worn on St Patrick's Day, and trefoil names any plant with three leaflets.

clue.text: Face coffee container?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a person's face
second meaning: a large cup with a handle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a verb for confronting your morning coffee; it is the slang noun for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal slang for someone's features and also the everyday name for a large handled drinking cup.

clue.text: Main character on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are only heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: the character is the letter C, pronounced like this

explanation.surface: The lead role in a radio drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main character' reads as the star of the show; 'Main' is the old poetic word for the ocean and 'character' is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary term for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main or 'the bounding main'.

clue.text: A little engraving on gold medal

indicators.note: a little of some words is a small run of their letters, lifted out intact

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, all of the second, and the first of the third

explanation.surface: A small inscription on a gold medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold medal' reads as a single phrase, but gold supplies only one letter and 'medal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British informal slang for a medal or official honour, such as a knighthood or an OBE.

clue.text: Sleeping accommodation rocks for rodents

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a shared bedroom
rocks is slang for ice cubes, as in a drink on the rocks

explanation.surface: Bedding made of stones for small animals to sleep on.
explanation.walkthrough: A drink served 'on the rocks' comes with ice, which is how rocks becomes ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small nocturnal rodents famous for long hibernation, the plural of dormouse.
